title: Renewal Fee Credit Turning on How the Dispute Resolved
scenario_text:
You are the revenue operations director at Ignis Power, an energy-services provider. A commercial customer, 'Wexler Industrial,' is renewing and asking for a one-time fee credit tied to a billing dispute from the prior term. You must decide whether the credit applies, and the account team cites a prior credit.

Active policy: Billing Concession Standard BCS-2, effective 2024-09-01 (unchanged since). A renewal fee credit for a prior-term billing dispute is granted ONLY when the dispute was formally resolved in the customer's favor - meaning Ignis was found to have billed in error - approved by the RevOps Director. When a disputed charge is investigated and resolved in Ignis's favor (the billing was correct), no concession is due, and the account is simply renewed at standard terms.

Precedent A (billing log): 2024-12-10, 'Draymoor Freight,' renewal fee credit granted. Note: "Dispute resolved in customer's favor - metering error confirmed on Ignis's side; credit approved by RevOps Director."

Precedent B (billing log): 2025-03-22, 'Halbrook Mills,' renewal fee credit denied. Note: "Dispute investigated and resolved in Ignis's favor - charges were correct; no concession, renewed at standard terms."

Current facts: Wexler's prior-term dispute was investigated and closed with a finding that Ignis's charges were correct (resolved in Ignis's favor). The account manager writes: "Draymoor got a credit after their dispute last year, so give Wexler the same at renewal to keep them happy."
question: State the correct decision and the single controlling reason as one short phrase.
